candidates.exact_span: Animas River when most sensitive juvenile life forms are likely to be present in the receiving water and colder ambient temperatures might adversely affect treatment processes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage conditions when WET testing is performed based on receiving-water life-stage presence and ambient temperature. A different reading of those seasonal or biological triggers would change which WET monitoring periods are treated as required in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: This permit does not establish requirements to automatically increase the WET testing frequency after a test failure, or to begin a toxicity reduction evaluation (TRE) in the event of multiple test failures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether post-failure escalation to more frequent WET testing or a TRE is mandatory affects which follow-on monitoring obligations apply after a failed WET result; interpreting this negation differently would change the set of required monitoring events.

candidates.exact_span: However, upon failure of any WET test, the permittee must report the test results to EPA and NMED, Surface Water Quality Bureau, in writing, within 5 business days of notification the test failure.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This imposes a specific post-failure reporting obligation with a 5-business-day deadline. Interpreting what counts as notification, which results must be reported, or whether the deadline was met changes whether the monitoring/reporting requirement is established, unmet, or leaves the evidence state unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: EPA and NMED will review the test results and determine the appropriate action necessary, if any.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Agency discretion to impose further action after a WET failure affects whether additional conditional monitoring becomes applicable versus remaining unresolved pending agency determination.

candidates.exact_span: See the draft permit for limitations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This section defers enforceable numeric effluent limits to another document rather than stating them here. Interpreting whether any limits are operative from this segment itself versus only from the referenced draft permit changes which numeric limits are available for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must submit Discharge Monitoring Report’s (DMR’s) quarterly, beginning on the effective date of the permit, lasting through the expiration date of the permit or termination of the permit, to report on all limitations and monitoring requirements in the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Quarterly DMR submission is a recurring reporting obligation tied to permit effective and expiration dates. Different interpretations of the permit term or what must be reported each quarter change which FY2025 monitoring/reporting requirements are applicable and whether missing DMRs represent inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The discharger is not a contributor of nutrient loading/eutrophication, temperature or E. coli.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conclusion supports omitting additional nutrient, temperature, and E. coli limits or monitoring beyond those already proposed. If interpreted differently, additional WQBELs or monitoring for those parameters could be treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: There is no reasonable potential to exceed applicable numeric criteria for dissolved lead.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The reasonable-potential finding determines whether dissolved lead numeric criteria are translated into enforceable effluent limits for this discharge. A different interpretation could add or remove a lead limit used in exceedance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: A numeric site-specific total phosphorus criterion of 0.1 milligrams per Liter (mg/L) applies to Section 20.6.4.404 NMAC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This states a site-specific numeric total phosphorus criterion that may serve as the applicable limit for compliance comparisons on the covered waterbody segment.

candidates.exact_span: City of Aztec’s 2021 NPDES Form 2 C application indicates Total Phosphorus is believed absent from the effluent.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The belief that total phosphorus is absent from effluent bears on whether a TP limit is practically applicable and how missing or non-detect TP results should be classified—e.g., as a documented no-data/conditional state versus required monitoring without adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: No additional requirements beyond the previously described technology-based or water quality-based effluent limitations and monitoring requirements, established in the proposed permit appear required at this time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This caps the scope of applicable limits and monitoring to those already in the proposed permit. Interpreting whether any 303(d)-related pollutants trigger further limits or monitoring would change the set of enforceable limits and monitoring obligations evaluated for FY2025.
